_doc: College story graph design (skeleton for review). Each entry becomes a draft in data/career/scenarios_college_graph.json once approved. 'sets' = flags its choices must set; 'requires.any_flags' = opened by; 'hs_callbacks' = high school flags read by a locked choice inside an open scene (light callbacks, never a gate); 'clears' = flags a choice sets to false. Flags are kept only where something reads them (a later scene, a locked choice, the finale or a planned pro scenario) or where they are a wrong-path strike; the other choices set no flag. pivot_flags: big choices (loyalty, honesty, partying, family, improper help, pressure) kept as flags for later college or pro callbacks.

scenarios.title: Move-In Day
scenarios.premise: {parent} helps you carry boxes into a cinderblock dorm room and lingers at the door longer than either of you expected.

scenarios.title: The First Team Meeting
scenarios.premise: {coach} lays out the rules on day one: curfew, study hall, phones in the bin at meetings, and one strike before the coach calls home.

scenarios.title: Far From Home
scenarios.premise: Three weeks in, the dining hall, the dorm and the practice field all feel like someone else's life, and nobody here knew you before.

scenarios.title: The Empty Group Chat
scenarios.premise: Your high school group chat goes quiet. {best_friend} posts photos from a new school with new friends, and you realize you haven't texted anyone in a week.

scenarios.title: The Roommate Draw
scenarios.premise: Your assigned roommate games until four in the morning, and your first lift is at six.

scenarios.title: Mandatory Study Hall
scenarios.premise: Your academic advisor, {teacher}, sets your schedule: six hours of study hall a week, signed in and out, or you lose eligibility.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Kicker
scenarios.premise: The senior kicker you're replacing next year can make your life easy or miserable, and he hasn't decided which.

scenarios.title: Walk-On Reality
scenarios.premise: You're paying your own way while scholarship players get meal cards and gear you don't. A teammate jokes that walk-ons are practice dummies.

scenarios.title: The Redshirt Teammate
scenarios.premise: A freshman kicker who's redshirting this year sits out every game and watches you kick. He's lonely, bitter, and good.

scenarios.title: The First Big Party
scenarios.premise: Upperclassmen throw the first big party of the year on a Thursday. The 6 a.m. lift is in seven hours, and everyone is watching what the freshmen do.

scenarios.title: Freshman Traditions
scenarios.premise: The seniors announce freshman duties: carry their bags, sing the fight song at dinner, fetch whatever they ask for.

scenarios.title: The Hazing Night
scenarios.premise: The freshman 'initiation' night arrives, and it's not singing anymore. Some of what the seniors have planned is humiliating, and some of it could hurt someone.

scenarios.title: Long Distance
scenarios.premise: {love_interest} is back home, the calls are getting shorter, and you keep missing each other between practice and class.

scenarios.title: The Holiday You Miss
scenarios.premise: The team practices straight through the holiday. {sibling} calls to ask why you're not coming home this year.

scenarios.title: First Road Trip
scenarios.premise: Your first road game: a hotel, a curfew check at eleven, and two upperclassmen planning to sneak out to a party across town.

scenarios.title: The Scholarship Fine Print
scenarios.premise: Your aid paperwork comes with a line you skipped: a minimum GPA to keep it. Midterms are in three weeks.

scenarios.title: The Pattern
scenarios.premise: You owned your first mistake, and the staff believed you. Now there's another one, and {coach} wants to know whether the first apology meant anything.
scenarios.note: Opens only on a strike after owning the first one (The Coach's Office clears strikes). The good choice sets owned_it_again and second_chance_used; the bad one sets character_concerns.

scenarios.title: The Sports Psychologist
scenarios.premise: The athletic department offers every player sessions with a sports psychologist. Most of the team jokes about it.

scenarios.title: Homecoming Weekend
scenarios.premise: Alumni pack the campus for homecoming. Boosters want photos, the band wants the specialists for a skit, and the team wants you rested.

scenarios.title: The Booster's Handshake
scenarios.premise: A friendly booster shakes your hand after practice and leaves something in it: a prepaid card 'for a nice dinner.'

scenarios.title: The First NIL Pitch
scenarios.premise: A local sandwich shop offers a small deal: free food all season and a few posts. It's legal, but it's your name on it.

scenarios.title: Budget Week
scenarios.premise: It's the middle of the semester and your account is nearly empty. Rent, books and a phone bill are due the same week.

scenarios.title: The Kicker You Know
scenarios.premise: {tyler} is a college kicker now too, and your names keep showing up next to each other on the same lists.

scenarios.title: The New Holder
scenarios.premise: Your new holder, {holder}, spins the laces a different way than you're used to, and neither of you wants to be the one to change.

scenarios.title: Sleepless Before Saturday
scenarios.premise: You haven't slept more than four hours before a game all season. You lie awake replaying kicks you haven't attempted yet.

scenarios.title: The Class You're Failing
scenarios.premise: A D on your chemistry midterm. Your advisor will see it Friday whether you tell them or not.

scenarios.title: Group Project Ghost
scenarios.premise: A teammate in your class wants his name on your group project. He hasn't come to a single meeting.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Talk
scenarios.premise: The senior captain pulls you aside: some of the guys think you act like you're too good for the team.

scenarios.title: The Highlight Clip
scenarios.premise: A trick-shot clip of you from practice goes around campus, and suddenly people you don't know want a picture.

scenarios.title: The Online Comment
scenarios.premise: A fan account tears into you after a loss. Your thumb is already on the reply button.

scenarios.title: {parent}'s Phone Call
scenarios.premise: {parent} sounds tired on the phone. His hours got cut, he says, but it's nothing for you to worry about.

scenarios.title: The Sibling Visit
scenarios.premise: {sibling} comes to campus for a weekend and wants to see everything: the locker room, the dorm, the parties he's heard about.

scenarios.title: The Upperclassman's Notes
scenarios.premise: An upperclassman offers you a folder of last year's exams for your hardest class. 'Everybody uses them,' he says.

scenarios.title: Winter Conditioning
scenarios.premise: Winter workouts start at 5:30 a.m. in the dark. Three teammates have already started skipping and signing each other in.

scenarios.title: Spring Kicking Competition
scenarios.premise: Spring practice opens with a kicking competition for next season. The veteran kicker is graduating, and the job is wide open.

scenarios.title: The Coach's Office
scenarios.premise: {coach} closes the door. Word of what you did got back to the staff, and the coach wants to hear it from you before deciding anything.

scenarios.title: The Tutor Who Offers More
scenarios.premise: Your tutor offers to 'clean up' your history paper. You both know that means writing it.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Prescription
scenarios.premise: Your hip is sore, and a teammate offers you some of his prescription. 'It's basically nothing,' he says.

scenarios.title: The Big House Party
scenarios.premise: An off-campus party gets out of hand fast. Campus security is on the way, and a teammate who's in bad shape can't find his ride.

scenarios.title: Hazing Fallout
scenarios.premise: The athletic department opens an investigation into last year's initiation night, and investigators want to talk to every sophomore.

scenarios.title: Now You're the Upperclassman
scenarios.premise: The new freshmen arrive, and the seniors look at your class. Freshman duties are yours to run now, or to end.

scenarios.title: The New Freshman Kicker
scenarios.premise: {coach} signs a scholarship freshman kicker, {backup}, and assigns them to share your reps and your locker row.

scenarios.title: The Position Battle
scenarios.premise: Fall camp turns into a public competition with {backup}. Every kick is charted, and the depth chart comes out Friday.

scenarios.title: The High School Tape
scenarios.premise: {coach} rewatches your old recruiting tape and stops on one clip. 'Tell me about this one,' the coach says.

scenarios.title: Did I Pick Right?
scenarios.premise: Friends at other schools look happier, and a teammate keeps talking about the transfer portal like it's an escape hatch.

scenarios.title: The Portal Call
scenarios.premise: A coach from another school calls you directly, which isn't allowed. He says there's a spot for you if you ever 'get curious.'

scenarios.title: The Sophomore Slump
scenarios.premise: Your practice charts are the worst they've been since high school, and you can't stop thinking about it, even in class.

scenarios.title: Panic in the Tunnel
scenarios.premise: Before warmups your chest goes tight, your hands won't stop shaking and you can't get a full breath.

scenarios.title: The Injury You Can't Hide
scenarios.premise: A groin strain flares on every kickoff. The trainer wants you out a week; the season says otherwise.

scenarios.title: The Training Table
scenarios.premise: A guy at the gym swears by a powder that isn't on the team's approved list. Two teammates already use it.

scenarios.title: The Visit Home
scenarios.premise: You go home for the first time in months. Your old room is a storage closet now, and everyone talks about people you don't know.

scenarios.title: Someone New
scenarios.premise: A classmate from your statistics class asks if you want to study together, and it doesn't feel like it's only about studying.

scenarios.title: The Best Friend's Crisis
scenarios.premise: {best_friend} calls at midnight: they're failing out of school and haven't told their family.

scenarios.title: {parent} Loses His Job
scenarios.premise: {parent} finally tells you: the cut hours became a layoff. He says he'll figure it out.

scenarios.title: The Collective
scenarios.premise: The school's NIL collective offers a monthly deal for appearances at booster events. It's real money, and it's a lot of evenings.

scenarios.title: The Loaner Car
scenarios.premise: A car dealer who sits behind the bench offers you a 'loaner' for the semester. No paperwork, he says.

scenarios.title: Conference Media Day
scenarios.premise: The team picks you to speak at conference media day, live, with a dozen microphones in your face.

scenarios.title: Rivalry Week
scenarios.premise: Rivalry week: someone painted your statue overnight, and teammates plan a midnight trip to the other campus to return the favor.

scenarios.title: The Alum in the League
scenarios.premise: A kicker from your school who made it to the pros offers to train you for a week this summer, at his own cost.

scenarios.title: The Summer Plan
scenarios.premise: Summer is three choices: summer classes to get ahead, a kicking camp circuit, or a job back home.

scenarios.title: The Holder Who Wants Out
scenarios.premise: {holder} wants to stop holding to focus on winning a starting job elsewhere on the roster.

scenarios.title: The Advisor's Warning
scenarios.premise: {teacher} calls you in: one more bad grade and you're academically ineligible.

scenarios.title: Hosting the Team Party
scenarios.premise: Your apartment is the obvious place for the team party, and everyone's already planning it.

scenarios.title: The Roommate Problem Grows
scenarios.premise: Your roommate's late nights have turned into parties in your room three nights a week.

scenarios.title: The Leadership Council
scenarios.premise: {coach} invites you onto the team's leadership council, the players who set the rules and handle the problems.

scenarios.title: The Head Coach Is Fired
scenarios.premise: The head coach is fired the morning after the last game. Staff jobs are up in the air, and half the roster is checking the portal.

scenarios.title: The Charity Kick-a-thon
scenarios.premise: A children's hospital asks the team to run a kick-a-thon fundraiser. Someone has to organize it.

scenarios.title: Spring Break
scenarios.premise: Teammates are going to the beach for spring break. Offseason lifts are optional that week, and so, it seems, are the rules.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Camp Coach
scenarios.premise: A private kicking coach who's sent players to the pros offers you a spot in his elite group, if you drop your school's summer program.

scenarios.title: The New Head Coach
scenarios.premise: The new head coach, Marcus Reyes, starts with a team meeting and a new rulebook. He says he's heard about every player on the roster already.

scenarios.title: The Second Strike
scenarios.premise: It happens again. This time it isn't only the coaches who know: a reporter is asking questions, and the team has to respond.
scenarios.note: Opens only on a strike AFTER the first warning: The Coach's Office clears every strike flag, so an old strike can't open it.

scenarios.title: The Runner
scenarios.premise: A man who says he works 'with' an agent finds you after practice with cash, a new phone and a promise of more.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Vote
scenarios.premise: The team votes for captains, and your name is on the ballot.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Burden
scenarios.premise: A teammate breaks team rules and asks you, as captain, to keep it in the locker room.

scenarios.title: The Scouting Questionnaire
scenarios.premise: A pro team sends a questionnaire. Question 14: 'Describe any off-field incidents in your college career.'

scenarios.title: The Agent's Dinner
scenarios.premise: An agent invites you to a steakhouse to 'talk about your future.' It's a year too early, and you both know the rules.

scenarios.title: The Transfer Kicker
scenarios.premise: A kicker with a big resume transfers in from another school, and the coaches love his leg.

scenarios.title: The Long Way Back
scenarios.premise: You've got a reputation now, and the staff is watching. {coach} offers one path back: early workouts, community hours, and no more excuses.

scenarios.title: The Mental Health Day
scenarios.premise: You're exhausted in a way sleep doesn't fix. The team counselor says taking a day isn't weakness.

scenarios.title: The Old Injury Returns
scenarios.premise: The groin strain is back, worse this time, right before the conference schedule.

scenarios.title: A High School Teammate Calls
scenarios.premise: Someone from your old high school team calls: they're visiting campus next weekend and need a place to stay and a tour.

scenarios.title: Trouble at Home
scenarios.premise: {sibling} got suspended from school for a fight. {parent} is overwhelmed and asks you to talk to him.

scenarios.title: {parent}'s Health Scare
scenarios.premise: A late-night call: {parent} is in the hospital. They think it's his heart, and you're four hundred miles away with a game Saturday.

scenarios.title: The Integrity Hearing
scenarios.premise: Your professor reports a possible academic integrity violation. The hearing is next week.

scenarios.title: Choosing a Major
scenarios.premise: You have to declare a major. One keeps you eligible with the least effort; another is the one you actually care about.

scenarios.title: The Final Warning
scenarios.premise: A third incident. {coach} and the head coach sit you down together: one more and you're off the team. This is the last conversation before that one.
scenarios.note: Opens on second_chance_used (set by the good choice in The Second Strike or The Pattern) plus a new strike. The good choice sets last_chance (no label, heavy cost); the bad one sets character_concerns. Either way, The Long Way Back stays open to anyone with the label.

scenarios.title: The Twenty-First Birthday
scenarios.premise: A teammate turns twenty-one on a Thursday and everyone is going out. Practice is at seven the next morning.

scenarios.title: The Viral Video
scenarios.premise: A teammate posts a video of you at a party, edited to look worse than it was. It's everywhere by morning.

scenarios.title: The Big Deal
scenarios.premise: A regional company offers a real NIL deal, but you'd have to promote a product you'd never use.

scenarios.title: The Tax Bill
scenarios.premise: Your NIL money came with a tax bill nobody warned you about, and it's due next month.

scenarios.title: The Ultimatum
scenarios.premise: {love_interest} wants you to spend the summer at home instead of at training camp. 'For once,' they say.

scenarios.title: Meeting the Family
scenarios.premise: The person you're dating wants you to meet their family over a holiday weekend, the same weekend as the team's leadership retreat.

scenarios.title: The Award Race
scenarios.premise: You and {tyler} are both finalists for the same national kicking award, and the media wants a feud.

scenarios.title: The Watch List
scenarios.premise: You make a preseason watch list for the top kicker in the country. Your phone won't stop.

scenarios.title: The Conference Title Race
scenarios.premise: Your team is in the conference title race, and the campus is out of its mind. Everyone wants a piece of the players this week.

scenarios.title: The Holder's Senior Day
scenarios.premise: It's {holder}'s last home game, and they ask you to walk out with their family on senior day.

scenarios.title: When the Alum Gets Cut
scenarios.premise: The pro kicker who trained you gets cut, and he calls you before he calls anyone else.

scenarios.title: Hosting a Recruit
scenarios.premise: {coach} asks you to host a high school kicker on an official visit. The recruit wants to see 'the real college experience.'

scenarios.title: A Teammate Enters the Portal
scenarios.premise: Your closest friend on the team enters the transfer portal without telling you first.

scenarios.title: The Late-Night Drive
scenarios.premise: After curfew, a teammate who's in no shape to drive wants to take everyone for food.

scenarios.title: Academic Honors
scenarios.premise: {teacher} says you're close to academic all-conference, if you take one more hard class instead of an easy elective.

scenarios.title: The Weight Room Push
scenarios.premise: The new strength coach wants you to add power fast. Your legs are already sore, and his program doesn't do rest days.

scenarios.title: The Leadership Retreat
scenarios.premise: The team's leaders spend a weekend at a lake planning next season. It's also your only free weekend of the summer.

scenarios.title: Senior Year Starts
scenarios.premise: The first practice of your last college season. Everyone keeps saying it goes fast.

scenarios.title: The Background Check
scenarios.premise: Pro scouts are interviewing everyone with a chance at the draft, and they've talked to people you haven't spoken to in years.
scenarios.note: Open to every senior; a locked choice for rebuilt_reputation ('the long way back') joins the high school callbacks.

scenarios.title: The Red Flag Interview
scenarios.premise: A scout sits across from you with a folder: everything that happened in college, in writing. 'Walk me through it,' he says.

scenarios.title: Choosing an Agent
scenarios.premise: Three agents want to represent you: a big firm, a former player, and a smooth talker promising a first-round grade.

scenarios.title: Combine Prep
scenarios.premise: A training facility offers to prepare you for the combine. Their 'recovery program' includes things you've never heard of.

scenarios.title: Pro Day
scenarios.premise: Your school's pro day is Thursday. The team's seniors are throwing a send-off party Wednesday night.

scenarios.title: Draft Weekend
scenarios.premise: Draft weekend is coming. Do you watch with family, with teammates, or with your phone off?

scenarios.title: The Degree Question
scenarios.premise: You're two classes from a degree. Dropping them would free up hours for draft training.

scenarios.title: Senior Night
scenarios.premise: Senior night, and your family is driving in. Before kickoff, the seniors walk out one at a time.

scenarios.title: The Last Rivalry Week
scenarios.premise: One last rivalry week. The younger players look to the seniors to set the tone.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Last Speech
scenarios.premise: {coach} asks you to speak to the team before the final game of your career.

scenarios.title: The Freshman Who Reminds You
scenarios.premise: A homesick freshman kicker reminds you of yourself four years ago.

scenarios.title: The Holder's Future
scenarios.premise: {holder} asks you for a recommendation for a graduate assistant job. It means writing honestly about someone you love working with.

scenarios.title: The Backup's Moment
scenarios.premise: You're sore, and {coach} wants to give {backup} the kickoffs this week. {backup} looks at you before saying yes.

scenarios.title: Old Rival, New Stage
scenarios.premise: {tyler} is entering the draft too, and his agent suggests you two train together for the combine.

scenarios.title: What Comes After
scenarios.premise: {love_interest} asks the question you've both avoided: what happens to us after college?

scenarios.title: {parent} at Every Game
scenarios.premise: {parent} has driven to every game this season. You know he can't afford it.

scenarios.title: The Little Brother's Recruiting
scenarios.premise: {sibling} is a high school senior now, and college coaches are calling. He asks you how to handle them.

scenarios.title: The Mental Toll
scenarios.premise: Draft season, final exams and your last season at once. You're short with everyone and you don't sleep.

scenarios.title: The Last Injury Scare
scenarios.premise: Your knee buckles on a routine practice kick three weeks before scouts arrive.

scenarios.title: Final Exams, Final Season
scenarios.premise: Your last finals land in the same week as your last regular-season game.

scenarios.title: The Senior Trip
scenarios.premise: Teammates book a senior trip in the middle of draft prep. It's the last time you'll all be together.

scenarios.title: The Exclusive Deal
scenarios.premise: A national brand wants an exclusive NIL deal for your senior year. It pays more than everything else combined, and it ends all your local deals.

scenarios.title: Giving Back
scenarios.premise: Your hometown asks if you'd run a free kicking camp for kids this summer. It would cost you a week and some of your NIL money.

scenarios.title: The Last Initiation
scenarios.premise: Your class is the senior class now. The freshman initiation is your call this year.

scenarios.title: The Scout's Dinner
scenarios.premise: A scout takes you to dinner and spends more time watching how you treat the waiter than asking about kicking.

scenarios.title: The Old Posts
scenarios.premise: Someone digs up your freshman-year posts during draft season and they're spreading.

scenarios.title: Conference Awards Night
scenarios.premise: You win an all-conference award. You have one minute at the podium.

scenarios.title: The Coach's Letter
scenarios.premise: {coach} is writing to pro scouts about you and asks what you want included, and what you'd rather leave out.

scenarios.title: The Last Practice
scenarios.premise: The last practice of your college career. The field is the same one you walked onto four years ago.

scenarios.title: The Roommate's Secret
scenarios.premise: Your roommate admits he hasn't left the room in days and asks you not to tell anyone.

scenarios.title: Sunday Night Blues
scenarios.premise: Every Sunday night the dorm goes quiet and you miss home most.

scenarios.title: The Group Chat Screenshot
scenarios.premise: A screenshot from the team group chat leaks, and a joke you laughed at is in it.

scenarios.title: The Parking Ticket Pile
scenarios.premise: Seven unpaid parking tickets and a hold on your registration.

scenarios.title: The Professor Who Doubts Athletes
scenarios.premise: A professor says, in front of the class, that athletes don't belong in her seminar.

scenarios.title: The Bus Argument
scenarios.premise: An argument on the team bus is turning personal, and two teammates are about to swing.

scenarios.title: The Fan Who Goes Too Far
scenarios.premise: A fan's messages have gone from friendly to strange. Now he says he knows where you live.

scenarios.title: Pickup Basketball
scenarios.premise: Teammates want you in a pickup basketball game. One rolled ankle could cost you a month.

scenarios.title: The Wrong Crowd
scenarios.premise: A group of non-team friends parties every night, and they've started inviting you along.

scenarios.title: The Borrowed Car
scenarios.premise: A teammate wants to borrow your car for the night and won't say where he's going.

scenarios.title: The Camp You Run
scenarios.premise: Parents offer you cash to run private kicking lessons for their kids this summer. Compliance has rules about that.

scenarios.title: The Aid Office Error
scenarios.premise: The financial aid office deposits twice what you're owed.

scenarios.title: The Extension
scenarios.premise: Team travel lands on a paper deadline. A teammate says the trick is to claim a family emergency.

scenarios.title: The Coach From Home
scenarios.premise: Your high school coach visits campus and wants to watch you practice.

scenarios.title: The Hospital Visit
scenarios.premise: The team visits a children's hospital. Some players are there for the cameras; one kid asks you to stay longer.

scenarios.title: The Weekend Off
scenarios.premise: Friends invite you away for a weekend off, your first in months.

scenarios.title: The Next Level
scenarios.premise: The last week of your college career. Whatever happens on draft day, this is where the kicker you became walks off the field.
scenarios.note: Locked choices: ready_for_pros needs combine_ready or pro_day_ready; life_after_football needs finished_degree_track; a rebuilt_reputation lock adds 'the long way back'; still_proving_it is open.
